result:
The proposed answer is incorrect. The correct order is β = 1/α, not 1/(1+α).

**Derivation.** Use the standard closed form of Sibson's mutual information:

I_α(X;Y) = (α/(α−1)) log ∫ (Σ_x p_x f_x(y)^α)^{1/α} dy,

where f_x(y) is the Gaussian density N(√snr·x, 1).

As snr → ∞, the Gaussians centered at different support points stop overlapping. At each y, only one term of the sum matters, so

(Σ_x p_x f_x(y)^α)^{1/α} ≈ Σ_x p_x^{1/α} f_x(y).

Each f_x integrates to 1, so the integral tends to Σ_x p_x^{1/α}. Therefore

I_α(X;Y) → (α/(α−1)) log Σ_x p_x^{1/α}.

The Rényi entropy of order β is H_β = (1/(1−β)) log Σ p_x^β. Setting β = 1/α gives 1/(1−1/α) = α/(α−1), which matches the limit exactly. So β = 1/α.

**Check at α = 1.** The correct formula gives β = 1, i.e. Shannon entropy, which matches the known high-SNR behavior of mutual information for discrete inputs. The proposed formula gives β = 1/2 at α = 1, which is wrong. The solution's own note even admits this inconsistency.

The proposed solution also uses an incorrect definition of Sibson's mutual information and gives no real derivation.

VERDICT: REJECT
